summary: Luke Badiali reviewed demand generation with Thomas Avery and Grace Lindqvist. Nearly all mandates arrive as short-notice RFPs from deal partners who already know Brookvale. We agreed a partner-to-partner outreach rhythm, a sector briefing series and an intermediary channel through sell-side corporate finance advisers.

discussion.keyPoints: Thomas's list showed 22 deal partners gave work in three years, and 9 of them gave 70 percent of it. New deal partners almost never appear.
Grace said sell-side corporate finance advisers choose the VDD provider on many processes, but Brookvale has relationships with only two.
Luke suggested quarterly sector briefings, which deal partners use when screening targets. Thomas worried about consultant time on non-billable work.

recommendations.recommendation: Thomas and Grace each to hold two breakfast meetings a month with deal partners not yet on the client list.
Add sell-side corporate finance advisers as a second channel, targeting 10 relationships by year end.
Publish a quarterly sector briefing for each of the three sectors, gated by email.
Host one deal partner dinner per sector each year with 10 guests.
Track pre-RFP conversations, aiming for 8 a month across the partners.

actions.action: Build a list of 40 corporate finance advisers active in mid-market healthcare and software sales

nextFocus: Tighten pitch execution so early conversations convert at a better rate.
nextPreparation: Grace to bring the scoping notes from two recent pitches.

tests.question: How many sell-side adviser relationships are we targeting?
Is the quarterly sector briefing agreed?
How concentrated is our deal partner base?
